featured_reviews.name: Durga
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review as an admitted patient who expected transparency, communication, and basic patient care, but unfortunately my experience raised several concerns.

One of my concerns involved the handling of medical supplies during my admission. I noticed items being taken away from my room and, when questioned, I was informed that these were being collected as replacements for items provided by the hospital. However, this process was never explained to me in advance. As a patient, I believe there should be complete transparency regarding any consumables, IV fluids, or medical supplies being used and accounted for, especially when these may ultimately be reflected in the final bill. I had to proactively raise this concern with the hospital administration myself.

My primary concern, however, was regarding the gastroenterology consultation. Throughout the day, I was repeatedly informed by the nursing staff that the gastroenterologist would be visiting me. Whenever I followed up, I was told that the doctor would come but that no one knew when. Even at around 9:30 PM, I was still waiting for clarity regarding the visit.

When I approached the reception desk for an update, I was informed that the gastroenterologist does not usually visit on Saturdays. This directly contradicted the information I had been receiving throughout the day. When I questioned why conflicting information had been provided, the RMO, Dr. Drishti, intervened in the conversation.

Unfortunately, my interaction with Dr. Drishti was disappointing. I found her communication to be dismissive and lacking empathy towards an admitted patient who was unwell and seeking clarity regarding their treatment. Rather than addressing my concern regarding the contradictory information provided by the staff, I was simply told that the doctor would come and that his timing was not fixed. No clear explanation was provided regarding the consultation process, expected timeline, or next steps. Additionally, at no point did the RMO assess my condition, enquire about my health status, or provide reassurance despite my repeated concerns.

It is with immense pain that I am writing this review after losing my grandmother at KEM Hospital, Parel. Our experience was deeply distressing and disappointing.

Throughout her treatment, we felt that the doctors were not fully transparent with us. We were repeatedly given hope about her recovery, and her condition was often described as stable or improving. However, her sudden deterioration left us shocked and confused. As a family, we now feel that we were not given a clear and honest picture of how critical her situation truly was.

In such sensitive moments, families deserve clarity, honesty, and realistic guidance — even if the truth is difficult. False reassurance or incomplete communication only makes the final loss more traumatic.

The staff nurses appeared inattentive and lacked empathy during crucial times. Communication was poor, and we often had to chase for updates. The management system felt disorganized, adding unnecessary stress to an already painful situation.

Hospitals are not only about treatment; they are about compassion, accountability, and dignity. Sadly, we did not feel that our grandmother received the level of transparency and care she deserved in her final days.

I hope the hospital administration reflects seriously on patient communication, staff behavior, and overall management practices so that other families do not go through what we experienced.

featured_reviews.name: Vibha Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience ever. Lost 15 years of trust in this hospital. Patients are being overcharged unnecessarily in the name of mediclaim. Special mention to Ms. Minakshi Bhat, Ms. Khot, and Dr. Anita Mayeker.

My daughter had a small infected cyst on her leg. Initially, she was able to walk normally, but even after antibiotics, the swelling increased. When the cyst burst and pus came out, we went back for dressing. Instead of simple treatment, we were pressured to admit her immediately for surgery and repeatedly asked about mediclaim.

The hospital quoted around ₹82,000 for treatment of a small cyst. The mediclaim company reportedly asked the hospital 4 times to explain such a high amount, but the hospital failed to provide proper clarification. Later, when the mediclaim company refused approval, the hospital suddenly reduced the amount to ₹71,500 for us to pay directly, again without explaining the charges or why there was a ₹10,500 difference after Mediclaim rejection.

We cancelled the surgery because the charges seemed unreasonable. For less than 24 hours of incomplete treatment, we still had to pay ₹13,000, which Mediclaim later refused to reimburse.

Very disappointing and stressful experience. It felt more focused on money than patient care, I will never ever recommend these doctors or this hospital to anyone.
